ln-falconborn.culture: Falconborn are the stooping raptor-aerie of the Skyward Isles, the fastest divers alive, prized as sky-couriers and hunters. Their aeries measure status by dive-speed, and a Falconborn's First Flight is a plunge between two isles that few forget.
ln-falconborn.tradition: The Stoop, a First Flight dive between drifting isles to earn adult wings.
ln-falconborn.appearance: Sharp-featured, swift-feathered in browns and greys, dive-harnesses.
ln-falconborn.naming: Given name plus a stoop-deed (Kael Swiftstoop).
ln-falconborn.landmark: Highperch, clinging to a drifting isle
hooks: A sinking isle holds your aerie and the lifeboats are few
A bridge was cut mid-stoop and you saw who did it
Your dive carried a message that started a sky-feud

ln-ravenkin.homeland: The market-quarter rookeries of the Crownlands cities
ln-ravenkin.culture: Ravenkin are the clever, secretive city-guild birdkin, keepers of the raven-lines' famous cunning and their hoards of stolen secrets. In every market a Ravenkin knows more than they say, and the legend of the Raven Who Stole a King's True Name is theirs.
ln-ravenkin.tradition: The Secret-Keeping, where a young Ravenkin earns standing by holding a dangerous secret without spending it.
ln-ravenkin.appearance: Black-feathered, sharp-eyed, dark clever finery, trinket-hoards.
ln-ravenkin.naming: Given name plus a wry epithet (Mattias Ninewords).
hooks: You hold a secret that could topple a guild and everyone knows you have it
A raven-line hoard was robbed of one specific thing
You may hold a fragment of the Nameless Emperor's true name

ln-swiftwing.homeland: The long sea-lanes of the Sapphire Sea
ln-swiftwing.environment: Open ocean and the endless trade-lanes
ln-swiftwing.culture: Swiftwings are the tireless long-distance birdkin, ocean-crossing navigators who crew the fleets and carry word between distant ports. No line flies farther without rest, and a Swiftwing's flock-songs map the whole Sapphire Sea from memory.
ln-swiftwing.tradition: The Long Crossing, a solo ocean flight out of sight of land to earn a navigator's mark.
ln-swiftwing.naming: Given name plus a crossing (Nera of the Long Blue).
hooks: A flock-song verse describes a route that no longer exists
You were first to spot the surfaced wreck on the Graveyard Reef
Your long crossing carried a message that must beat a storm home

ln-stormcrow.homeland: The storm-belt roosts of the Stormreach
ln-stormcrow.environment: The living storm-front and lightning-lashed coasts
ln-stormcrow.culture: Stormcrows ride the tempest, birdkin who take no penalty in the wind and are read as omens by the storm-cults. Where a Stormcrow gathers, the Stormwardens say, the Storm is watching, and their flock-cries are treated as weather-augury.
ln-stormcrow.tradition: The Storm-Cry, where a young Stormcrow flies into a tempest and returns to speak what the Storm showed.
ln-stormcrow.naming: Given name plus a storm-omen (Grael Tempestcry).
rivals: Stormwardens (who both use and fear them)
hooks: Your flock gathered over a hold and now it fears an omen
The Storm showed you something in a storm-cry you can't forget
The Standing Bolt is dying and the crows are fleeing it

ln-sunfeather.homeland: The oasis market-quarters of the Sunscorch
ln-sunfeather.culture: Sunfeathers are the bright-plumed dawn-birds of the desert towns, birdkin whose dazzling display can blind a foe and whose songs open the oasis-markets each dawn. They are the criers, entertainers, and daybreak-heralds of the Sunscorch.
ln-sunfeather.tradition: The Dawn-Song, sung at first light to open the market and mark the singer as come-of-age.
ln-sunfeather.appearance: Brilliant gold-and-crimson plumage, sun-bright, festival finery.
ln-sunfeather.naming: Given name plus a dawn-name (Isha Dawnsong).
rivals: Those who work in the dark
hooks: Your dawn-song is the only thing keeping a market's fragile peace
A rival crier is spreading a false omen in your voice
Your dazzle blinded the wrong person and now you owe a debt

ln-bird-raven.environment: The twilight fortress-city and its long-shadowed towers
ln-bird-raven.culture: The true Raven-line keeps the oldest secret-hoards, dwelling among the night-courts as brokers of forbidden knowledge. Older and darker than their Crownlands Ravenkin cousins, they trade in the secrets the living would rather forget.
ln-bird-raven.tradition: The Naming-Theft, a rite of learning one secret so dangerous the whole roost must keep it.
ln-bird-raven.appearance: Glossy black, red-tinged eyes, shadow-silk finery.
ln-bird-raven.naming: Given name plus a taken secret (Corvain Blacktongue).
hooks: You hold a secret the Night Court would kill to bury
The Unlit want a name only your roost remembers
A stolen secret in your hoard is worse than you knew

ln-bird-crow.homeland: The old battlefields and gallows-fields of the Crownlands
ln-bird-crow.culture: Crow-line birdkin keep the field-rites, gathering where the Old Empire's dead lie and remembering the fallen no one else will name. Wrongly called ill omens, they are in truth the mourners and memory-keepers of the war-country.
ln-bird-crow.tradition: The Field-Watch, a rite of standing vigil over unburied dead until they are named.
ln-bird-crow.appearance: Sooty black, watchful, mourning-grey wraps, field-tokens.
ln-bird-crow.naming: Given name plus a field (Wren of Ashenfield).
ln-bird-crow.landmark: The Ashfall Road paved with the bones of an army
hooks: A war-field you watch has begun to give up its dead
You know where an imperial vault lies beneath the fallen
A sunder-wight has risen following your field-watch

ln-bird-eagle.homeland: The high crag-aeries of the Ironspine peaks
ln-bird-eagle.environment: The highest mountain crags above the cloud line
ln-bird-eagle.culture: Eagle-line birdkin hold the proudest highland aeries, sky-lords who claim the peaks and look down, often literally, on the ground-bound. Fierce and honor-bound, they guard the high passes alongside the goliath clans.
ln-bird-eagle.tradition: The High-Claiming, a first flight to the highest crag one can reach, marking one's standing.
ln-bird-eagle.naming: Given name plus a peak (Aquila of the Ninth Crag).
ln-bird-eagle.landmark: The Nine Bridges above the cloud line
hooks: A roc has taken the crag your aerie claims
A vault-war on the peaks threatens your high pass
Your pride will not let you fly with the ground-bound, and you must

ln-bird-falcon.homeland: The falconry-courts of the Sunscorch oases
ln-bird-falcon.culture: Falcon-line birdkin are the desert hunt-partners and messengers, bonded to the caravan-courts as scouts and swift-flyers. Distinct from the sky-isle Falconborn, they keep the oasis-roads watched and the sun-courts informed.
ln-bird-falcon.tradition: The Bonding, a rite where a young Falcon pledges partnership to a caravan or court for a season.
ln-bird-falcon.appearance: Barred grey-and-tan, sharp, court-liveried jesses and charms.
ln-bird-falcon.naming: Given name plus a court (Sef of the Sun Court).
hooks: The court you bonded to sends you into the deep dunes
You carry warning of a raid the court will not believe
Your bonded caravan uncovered a buried city

ln-bird-hawk.homeland: The frontier watch-towers of the Crownlands marches
ln-bird-hawk.environment: Open country, farmland, and border watch-posts
ln-bird-hawk.culture: Hawk-line birdkin are the borderland sentinels, sharp-eyed watchers who guard the frontier roads and farmsteads. Practical and vigilant, they are the eyes of many a Crownlands duchy and rarely miss what moves below.
ln-bird-hawk.tradition: The First Watch, a solo vigil over a stretch of border to earn a sentinel's post.
ln-bird-hawk.naming: Given name plus a watch-post (Talia of Ashford Watch).
ln-bird-hawk.landmark: The frontier watch-towers of the Crownlands
hooks: You spotted an army the duchy insists is not there
Your border-post has gone silent one tower at a time
A message-hawk route has been compromised

ln-bird-osprey.homeland: The coastal fishing-towns of the Sapphire Sea
ln-bird-osprey.culture: Osprey-line birdkin are the fisher-hunters of the coasts, diving birdkin who bring in the catch and pilot boats through the reef-shallows. They are the backbone of the fishing-fleets and read the water as well as any seaborn.
ln-bird-osprey.tradition: The First Dive, plunging for one's first catch in the reef-shallows to join the fleet.
ln-bird-osprey.naming: Given name plus a shoal (Marl of the Coral Shoal).
ln-bird-osprey.landmark: The Graveyard Reef where sunk fleets rest
hooks: The reef-serpents are driving the fish, and the fleets, ashore
Your fishing-ground was seized by the covenant
You dived on a wreck and brought up more than fish

ln-bird-swan.environment: Moonlit lakes and mist-gardens of the Vale
ln-bird-swan.culture: Swan-line birdkin are the graceful court-birds of the Vale, keepers of ceremony, beauty, and the old courtesies. Elegant and proud, they preside over the Moon Court's rites, and a Swan's disfavor can end a courtier's season.
ln-bird-swan.tradition: The Lake-Dance, a coming-of-age performance on the moonlit water before the court.
ln-bird-swan.naming: Given name plus a lake (Odila of Silvermere).
hooks: A Moon Court ceremony you preside over hides a deadly plot
Your grace-favor is being forged to ruin a rival
The lake showed you a fate mid-dance

ln-bird-heron.homeland: The marsh-villages at the Wilds' waterways
ln-bird-heron.culture: Heron-line birdkin are the patient marsh-folk, still-standing hunters and reed-lore keepers of the wetland Wilds. Contemplative and solitary-leaning, they are sought as healers and quiet counselors who wait out any trouble.
ln-bird-heron.tradition: The Still-Watch, standing motionless in the marsh until the reeds accept you, marking adulthood.
ln-bird-heron.naming: Given name plus a fen (Sedge of the Grey Marsh).
ln-bird-heron.landmark: The reed-country of the Emerald Wilds
hooks: A blight is creeping through your marsh
Your reed-lore is the only cure for a spreading sickness
Something old has risen in the fen you watch

ln-bird-parrot.homeland: The bright island-ports of the Sapphire Sea
ln-bird-parrot.culture: Parrot-line birdkin are the polyglot traders and tale-tellers of the island-ports, birdkin who speak every tongue of the sea and carry news, gossip, and languages between a hundred harbors. No deal in Port Meridian closes without one nearby.
ln-bird-parrot.tradition: The Hundred-Words, learning to greet in a hundred tongues before joining the harbor-guild.
ln-bird-parrot.naming: Given name plus a port (Rio of Port Meridian).
hooks: You overheard a deal in a tongue no one knew you spoke
A rumor you carried has sparked a harbor-war
You alone can translate a covenant ultimatum

ln-bird-songbird.homeland: The market-quarters of the Crownlands cities
ln-bird-songbird.environment: City squares, guild-halls, and festival streets
ln-bird-songbird.culture: Songbird-line birdkin fill the cities with music and news, birdkin whose songs carry history, gossip, and the mood of the streets. A Songbird's tune can raise a festival or a riot, and criers, minstrels, and heralds spring from their line.
ln-bird-songbird.tradition: The First Song, a public performance in the market square to earn a singer's name.
ln-bird-songbird.naming: Given name plus a song (Lark of the Lantern Ward).
hooks: Your song stirred a riot the guilds want blamed on you
A forbidden verse of history is yours alone to sing
A rival is stealing your songs to spread a lie

ln-bird-vulture.homeland: The ash-roads and ruin-fields of the Ashen Wastes
ln-bird-vulture.culture: Vulture-line birdkin keep the death-rites others shun, birdkin who tend the fallen and cleanse the ash-fields of the dead. Feared and misunderstood, they are in truth sacred undertakers, and no ash-clan buries its dead without a Vulture's blessing.
ln-bird-vulture.tradition: The Cleansing, a rite of tending the unburied dead so they do not rise as ash-wraiths.
ln-bird-vulture.naming: Given name plus a rite-name (Morrec Ashkeeper).
ln-bird-vulture.landmark: The Glass Capital and its unburied dead
hooks: Ash-wraiths are rising where a cleansing was skipped
You must give death-rites to an enemy to stop them rising
A vault in the Glass Capital holds unblessed dead

ln-bird-magpie.homeland: The thieves'-markets and undercity of the Crownlands
ln-bird-magpie.culture: Magpie-line birdkin are the collectors and cat-burglars, birdkin who cannot resist a shining thing and turn it into a trade. Charming and light-fingered, they run the grey-markets and fence what falls off the back of a wagon.
ln-bird-magpie.tradition: The First Find, a rite of acquiring, by wit or worse, one shining thing to start a hoard.
ln-bird-magpie.appearance: Black-and-white, glittering with trinkets, pocketed finery.
ln-bird-magpie.naming: Given name plus a prized find (Pica Brightpocket).
ln-bird-magpie.landmark: The Grey Market of the undercity
hooks: You stole a shining thing that turned out to be cursed
A powerful person wants back exactly what you fenced
Your hoard holds a key someone will kill for

ln-bird-crane.homeland: The garden-shrines of the Moonlit Vale
ln-bird-crane.environment: Misted gardens, shrine-pools, and quiet groves
ln-bird-crane.culture: Crane-line birdkin are the long-lived shrine-keepers and peacemakers of the Vale, birdkin of ceremony, patience, and the sacred art of the folded oath. A Crane's mediation is trusted across the Vale, and their dances are said to bless a long life.
ln-bird-crane.tradition: The Folded Oath, a ceremony where promises are sealed in an intricate ritual dance.
ln-bird-crane.appearance: Tall, white-and-red crowned, ceremonial robes, oath-folds.
ln-bird-crane.naming: Given name plus a shrine (Tsuru of the Nine Lanterns).
hooks: A folded oath you sealed is being broken and blamed on you
One of the Nine Lanterns went dark during your ceremony
You must mediate a feud that wants no peace

ln-bird-seagull.homeland: The rough dock-quarters of every sea-port
ln-bird-seagull.culture: Seagull-line birdkin are the scrappy, adaptable dock-folk, birdkin who thrive in every harbor and turn any scrap into a living. Loud, clever, and impossible to be rid of, they are the sailors, scavengers, and rumor-mills of the waterfront.
ln-bird-seagull.tradition: The Scavenging, a rite of surviving a season on the docks by wit alone to earn a berth.
ln-bird-seagull.naming: Given name plus a dock (Skip of Saltmarket).
hooks: A dock-rumor you spread turned out to be dangerously true
You scavenged something a captain will kill to reclaim
A blockade is starving the docks and you know a way out

ln-bird-peacock.homeland: The sun-courts and pleasure-gardens of Sunspire
ln-bird-peacock.culture: Peacock-line birdkin are the resplendent court-birds of the sun-courts, birdkin of display, fashion, and elaborate status-games. Vain by reputation and shrewd in truth, they turn beauty into influence and rule the Sunscorch's salons.
ln-bird-peacock.tradition: The Unfurling, a debut display before the court where a young Peacock claims their status.
ln-bird-peacock.appearance: Iridescent blue-green trains, jeweled finery, display-marks.
ln-bird-peacock.naming: Given name plus a court-house (Mayur of House Sunfeather).
hooks: Your court debut exposed a plot against the Sun Court
A rival is spreading a scandal in your name
The lost heir was last seen at your salon

ln-bird-hummingbird.homeland: The flower-groves and Meadowborn villages of the Wilds' edge
ln-bird-hummingbird.culture: Hummingbird-line birdkin are the tiny, tireless pollinators and swift messengers of the flower-country, birdkin whose speed and delicacy make them prized couriers and healers. Small but fierce, they defend their groves with startling boldness.
ln-bird-hummingbird.tradition: The Nectar-Run, a swift First Flight visiting nine blossoming groves in a single day.
ln-bird-hummingbird.naming: Given name plus a bloom (Zip of the Ninth Blossom).
ln-bird-hummingbird.landmark: The wildflower meadows of the Wilds' edge
hooks: A blight is killing the groves your nectar-run depends on
You carry a healing-nectar someone desperately needs
Your grove is threatened and you will not flee it

ln-bird-woodpecker.homeland: The timber-holds and forest-towns of the Emerald Wilds
ln-bird-woodpecker.culture: Woodpecker-line birdkin are the carpenters and forest-craftfolk, birdkin whose knock-signals carry through the trees and whose woodcraft shapes the Wilds' towns. Industrious and precise, they read a tree's health by its sound and keep the timber-truce with the Greenwardens.
ln-bird-woodpecker.tradition: The Knock-Speech, learning the tapped signal-code that carries messages across the forest.
ln-bird-woodpecker.naming: Given name plus a grove (Tock of Thornwatch).
hooks: The knock-code carried a distress signal you must answer
A sickness in the timber only your ear can find
Loggers are breaking the timber-truce your line keeps

ln-bird-pelican.homeland: The provisioning-ports and island stores of the Sapphire Sea
ln-bird-pelican.culture: Pelican-line birdkin are the carriers and provisioners of the sea-trade, big-billed birdkin who haul supplies, run relief to storm-struck isles, and keep the fleets fed. Generous and dependable, they are the quiet logistics that keep the Sapphire Sea alive.
ln-bird-pelican.tradition: The Carrying, a rite of running relief-supplies to a distant isle without loss.
ln-bird-pelican.naming: Given name plus a depot (Bram of Coralhold Stores).
hooks: A storm-struck isle will starve without your relief-run
Raiders have hit your supply-depot
Your relief cargo hid contraband you knew nothing about

ln-bird-cardinal.homeland: The winter-holds of the Frostbound North
ln-bird-cardinal.culture: Cardinal-line birdkin are the winter-heralds of the north, bright-red birdkin whose appearance marks the turning seasons and whose songs carry ancestor-omens across the snow. Steadfast in the cold, they are the north's messengers of hope and warning alike.
ln-bird-cardinal.tradition: The Winter-Herald, a song sung at the deep of winter to call the ancestors' guidance.
ln-bird-cardinal.appearance: Brilliant crimson against the snow, crest-marked, ancestor-charms.
ln-bird-cardinal.naming: Given name plus a winter (Ember of the Long White).
hooks: Your winter-herald song foretold a doom the hold denies
You must carry hope to a hold the Winter Hunt has cut off
An ancestor-omen named you for a hard task

ln-bird-bluejay.homeland: The town-squares and frontier villages of the Crownlands
ln-bird-bluejay.environment: Market-towns, village greens, and woodland edges
ln-bird-bluejay.culture: Blue Jay-line birdkin are the bold, brash alarm-callers and mimics, birdkin who raise the cry when trouble comes and can throw any voice they have heard. Clever tricksters and fierce defenders, they are the self-appointed sentinels of a hundred small towns.
ln-bird-bluejay.tradition: The Alarm-Cry, a rite of proving one can raise, and be trusted with, the town's warning-call.
ln-bird-bluejay.naming: Given name plus a town (Jai of Ashford).
ln-bird-bluejay.landmark: The village greens of the Crownlands
hooks: You raised an alarm no one believed until too late
You can mimic a voice that could expose or frame a lord
A false alarm in your voice has ruined your name
